proposals.before: At nine he followed his father's elder brother Kan to call on Minister of Rites Lu Yan. Yan asked ten points on the Five Classics; Li answered each without miss, and Yan marveled.
proposals.after: At nine, he accompanied his father's elder cousin Chan on a visit to Chamberlain for Ceremonials Lu Chui. Chui asked him ten questions on the Five Classics; Li answered each without error, and Chui marveled at him.
proposals.reason: 從伯闡 is his father's elder cousin Chan, 太常 is the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and 陸倕 is Lu Chui (Chuí), not Lu Yan.

proposals.before: At age nine he followed his father's elder brother Kan to call on the Minister of Rites Lu Yan; Yan asked ten matters on the Five Classics and Li answered each question as asked, missing nothing—Yan marveled at him.
proposals.after: At age nine, he accompanied his father's elder cousin Chan to call on the Chamberlain for Ceremonials Lu Chui; Chui asked ten questions concerning the Five Classics, and Li answered each as it was put to him without missing anything. Chui marveled at him.
proposals.reason: 從伯闡 is his father's elder cousin Chan, 太常 is the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and 陸倕 is Lu Chui rather than Lu Yan in the literal English as well.

proposals.before: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan summoned him as secretariat gentleman and Marquis of Zhenyang and made him vice governor of Yangzhou; he accepted none of it.
proposals.after: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan summoned him as secretariat gentleman; the Marquis of Zhenyang offered him appointment as vice governor of Yangzhou; he accepted none of it.
proposals.reason: 貞陽侯 is a separate actor (Xiao Yuanming), not a title conferred on Yu Li; the translation fuses the two appointments.

proposals.before: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Secretariat Gentleman and Marquis of Zhenyang, and appointed him Vice Governor of Yangzhou—all of which he did not accept.
proposals.after: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Secretariat Gentleman; the Marquis of Zhenyang appointed him Vice Governor of Yangzhou—none of which he accepted.
proposals.reason: Chinese 貞陽侯，授揚州別駕 names the Marquis as the one granting the Yangzhou post, not Yu Li as Marquis.

proposals.before: After Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied the slaughter of his household and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with five hundred households.
proposals.after: After Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied that his wife and children had been slaughtered, and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with five hundred households.
proposals.reason: 妻子嬰戮 means wife and children were slaughtered (嬰戮), not that children were infants named Ziying; keep the sense of household slaughter without the false personal name.

proposals.before: Several schools of scholars each raised questions. Shu answered in turn, opened each main point, then branched into endless distinctions; the debaters bowed and listened in silence. Lun was greatly pleased.
proposals.after: Several schools of scholars each raised questions. Shu answered in turn, opened each main point, then branched into endless distinctions; the debaters bowed and listened in silence.
proposals.reason: Chinese for this unit ends at 聽受而已; 綸甚嘉之 belongs to the next sentence and was wrongly fused into the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Thereupon several families of scholars each rose to pose questions; Shu then in sequence analyzed and judged, opening their main points, then branching into streams and divisions, turning and changing without end; the debaters bowed in silence and only listened—Lun greatly praised him.
proposals.after: Thereupon several families of scholars each rose to pose questions; Shu then in sequence analyzed and judged, opening their main points, then branching into streams and divisions, turning and changing without end; the debaters bowed in silence and only listened.
proposals.reason: The clause Lun greatly praised him translates 綸甚嘉之, which is the start of the following unit, not this one.

proposals.before: Lun meant to recommend him at court.
proposals.after: Lun greatly praised him and meant to recommend him at court.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 甚嘉之 after that praise was wrongly moved into the previous unit.

proposals.before: Shu read through them almost entirely and sighed: "I hear that men who prize office take Chao and Jufu as shackles, and men who love the hills take Yi and Lü as storekeepers; those who bind name to fact treat Zhuangzi as straw, and those who play at emptiness treat banquet talk as chaff. In earnest judgment each follows his own bent.
proposals.after: Shu read through them almost entirely and sighed: "I hear that men who prize office take Chao Fu and Xu You as shackles, and men who love the hills take Yi and Lü as storekeepers; those who bind name to fact treat Laozi as straw, and those who play at emptiness treat banquet talk as chaff. In earnest judgment each follows his own bent.
proposals.reason: 巢、由 are the recluses Chao Fu and Xu You, while 柱下之言 refers to Laozi (柱下史), not Zhuangzi.

proposals.before: Shu with full intent searched and read them, nearly covering all; he then sighed and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and title take Chao and Jufu as fetters, and those who love mountains and forests take Yi and Lü as granary keepers; binding name and reality makes Zhuangzi's words mere hay; playing with emptiness and purity makes seat-side doctrines mere chaff; checked against earnest discourse, each also follows his own preference.
proposals.after: Shu with full intent searched and read them, nearly covering all; he then sighed and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and title take Chao Fu and Xu You as fetters, and those who love mountains and forests take Yi and Lü as granary keepers; binding name and reality makes Laozi's words mere hay; playing with emptiness and purity makes seat-side doctrines mere chaff; checked against earnest discourse, each also follows his own preference.
proposals.reason: 巢、由 are Chao Fu and Xu You, while 柱下之言 is Laozi's words (柱下史), so Zhuangzi's words is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: Beside men who seek resolve today, they stop at the roadside and turn back.
proposals.after: Compared with men of resolve, today's seekers gaze at the road and give up.
proposals.reason: 比求志之士 contrasts ancient exemplars with present seekers who look at the path and stop; the current idiomatic reverses the comparison.

proposals.before: When the prince of Poyang was inspector of South Xuzhou, he admired Shu's loftiness but could not summon him; he used humble words and rich courtesy and sent envoys again and again, but Shu firmly pleaded illness.
proposals.after: When the prince of Poyang was inspector of South Xuzhou, he admired Shu's loftiness and was ashamed he could not summon him; he used humble words and rich courtesy and sent envoys again and again, but Shu firmly pleaded illness.
proposals.reason: 鄙不能致 means he despised or was ashamed of his inability to bring Shu, not merely that he could not summon him.

decisions.reason: s0070 從伯闡 is the father's elder cousin Chan, 太常 is Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and 陸倕 is Lu Chui; “elder brother Kan,” “Minister of Rites,” and “Lu Yan” are naming and office errors, and the proposed English matches the Chinese.
The same Chinese errors appear in the literal field: 從伯闡, 太常, and 陸倕 require “father's elder cousin Chan,” “Chamberlain for Ceremonials,” and “Lu Chui,” not Kan, Minister of Rites, or Lu Yan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 從伯闡候太常陸倕，倕問五經凡有十事

decisions.reason: s0081 元帝徵為中書侍郎，貞陽侯，授揚州別駕 names two actors: Emperor Yuan summons him as secretariat gentleman, then the Marquis of Zhenyang grants the Yangzhou post; the before text wrongly treats 貞陽侯 as Yu Li's title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元帝徵為中書侍郎，貞陽侯，授揚州別駕，並不就

decisions.reason: Literal 貞陽侯，授揚州別駕 likewise makes the Marquis the granter of 揚州別駕, not a marquisate conferred on Yu Li; the proposed split correctly restores agency and 並不就.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 貞陽侯，授揚州別駕，並不就

decisions.reason: s0018 妻子嬰戮 means his wife and children were slaughtered; “household” is broader than 妻子 and less precise after s0017 already names wife and son, so the proposed wording is the accurate repair.
s0255 ends at 聽受而已; 綸甚嘉之 belongs to s0256, so “Lun was greatly pleased” is fused from the next unit and must be removed from this idiomatic sentence.
The literal clause “Lun greatly praised him” translates 綸甚嘉之, which opens s0256, not s0255; deleting it restores the unit boundary at 聽受而已.
s0256 is 綸甚嘉之，將引薦於朝廷; after removing the praise from s0255, the idiomatic must restore 甚嘉之 here, and the proposed sentence does so without inventing content.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 綸甚嘉之，將引薦於朝廷

decisions.reason: 巢、由 are Chao Fu and Xu You, not “Chao and Jufu,” and 柱下之言 points to Laozi as 柱下史, not Zhuangzi; the proposed names correct both mistranslations.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 貴爵位者以巢、由為桎梏……芻芥柱下之言

decisions.reason: The literal shares the same errors: 巢、由 and 柱下之言 require Chao Fu, Xu You, and Laozi’s words, so replacing Jufu and Zhuangzi is required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 巢、由為桎梏……芻芥柱下之言

decisions.reason: After the ancient exemplars in s0259, 比求志之士，望塗而息 contrasts those men of resolve with present seekers who gaze at the path and stop; the before text reverses that comparison.
s0265 鄙不能致 adds the prince’s shame or disdain at failing to bring Shu; “but could not summon him” drops 鄙, and “was ashamed he could not summon him” restores that sense.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0001 shows “Lu Yan” was invented by misreading 陸倕; the person is Lu Chui, already recorded in c0124, so the Yan name claim has no source support.

claimRevisions.reason: 闡 romanizes as Chan, not Kan; r0001 restores the correct English personal name while keeping the same Chinese graph.
从伯 is father's elder cousin, and 闡 is Chan; the descriptive-kinship English must match the repaired translation.
倕 is Chui, not Yan; r0001 corrects the given-name claim to the reading supported by 陸倕.
从伯 marks a collateral paternal uncle (father's elder cousin), so the kinship term and relation to the father must change from elder brother / sibling-of to elder cousin / cousin-of.
由 is You (Xu You); “Jufu” was created by the bad idiomatic naming that r0009 replaces, while the Xu You alias in c0334 remains valid.
